context: FASE 1-4 of the token economy initiative implemented context filtering (engine), summarization (runner), token budget protection (runner), and telemetry (runner). These operate at runtime with defaults and agent-level config. FASE 5 requires per-node budget control in the workflow definition itself, allowing workflow authors to declare explicit token budgets per step based on the step's complexity and risk.
problem: How to add per-node token budget control to the workflow schema without breaking existing workflows, while maintaining backward compatibility and the deterministic execution model?

options_considered.option: Add required max_context_tokens field to node schema
cons: Forces authors to estimate tokens upfront

options_considered.option: Add optional max_context_tokens field with default from agent config
pros: Falls back to agent-level then global default

options_considered.option: Add max_context_tokens at workflow level only
cons: Too coarse; different nodes need different budgets

decision: Add optional `max_context_tokens` field to workflow node schema (integer, minimum 256). When present, it overrides the agent's llm_config.max_tokens for that specific node's context budget calculation. When absent, the agent's llm_config.max_tokens (default 4096) is used. The 70% budget rule (FASE 2) applies to the resolved max_tokens. Schema version remains 1 (additive optional field).
reason: Optional field preserves backward compatibility. Default chain (node > agent > global) gives flexibility. The 70% rule in runner remains unchanged — only the input max_tokens changes. No new runtime mechanisms needed.
consequences: Existing workflows validate and run unchanged. New workflows can opt-in to per-node budgets. Engine passes resolved max_tokens to AgentRunner. Tests updated to cover both paths. No migration required.
